idea.title: 3 snack vending machines in offices and gyms

source.text: Buying 3 snack vending machines and placing them in offices and gyms. Launch country US, budget $10,000, 8 hours a week, goal side income, no special edge. Just go: do not ask questions.

idea.customer: Office workers and gym members (via office and gym hosts)
idea.solution: Buy 3 snack vending machines and place them in offices and gyms
assumptions: Used machines (~$2,645 each) with cashless readers, not new
Snacks bought at warehouse clubs, sold at ~2x cost
No prior vending, sales or repair experience
Single US metro area, owner restocks weekly by car

confidence.note: Per-machine revenue rests on a 2020 survey of 23 operators; real sales data from local office and gym sites would raise it.

gross_margin.note: ~31% after 50% COGS, 10% commission, ~4.8% card fees, 4% shrink (estimate). Under 30% = 1. R5 costs_eat_margin.

ltv_cac.note: LTV $3,448 vs $3,334 per placed machine = 1.03; 0.49 after per-machine fixed costs. Fix path: only high-traffic sites.

pricing_power.note: Snack prices anchored by stores; locations expect free placement plus 5-25% commission. Card surcharge is the only lever.

build_effort.note: Nothing to build: buy a used machine, stock from Sam's Club, place it. 2-4 weeks.

skills_match.note: No stated vending, sales or repair skills; all learnable, but cold prospecting is the hard part.

capital_needed.note: 3 used machines + readers + stock = ~$9,900 of a $10,000 budget; no buffer for insurance or repairs.

time_to_mvp.note: ~4 weeks: find a site, buy and move a used machine, get a sales tax permit (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Office or gym manager decides in 1-4 weeks; property managers may require insurance certificates.

channel_readiness.note: Channel exists (walk-ins, cold calls) but user has none; operators report 100+ calls per decent site.

search_demand.note: Daily snack habit, but host demand is weak: offices run ~54% of pre-pandemic occupancy.

trend.note: US vending operators -1.3% in 2025, -0.3%/yr 2020-2025 (IBISWorld). R5 weak_demand.

willingness_to_pay.note: Buyers pay per vend, but hosts pay $0 and expect commission; per-machine gross ~$309/month.

free_alternatives.note: Hosts get free full-service vending from any operator; employees can also bring snacks or use pantries.

competitor_density.note: Local operators, national Canteen (Compass) and micro markets all pitch the same breakrooms. R5 strong_competitor.

differentiation.note: Same machines, same snacks, no edge. Micro markets and smart coolers out-feature a used spiral machine.

legal_regulatory.note: Sales tax permit, local business licence; health permit only for some food. Light compliance.

platform_dependency.note: Each site's host can remove you at will; card processor terms set fees. Alternatives exist.

market_risk.note: Structural, not cyclical: hybrid work and micro markets shrink office vending.

skills.note: No relevant skills stated (route ops, sales, machine repair).

assets.note: No audience, network or locations: 'no special edge'.

interest.note: Goal is side income: the money, not the domain.

sam.reasoning: $7.7bn x 1.5% (one metro's share of US population, assumed) x 50% snack share (assumed) = ~$58M

competitors_found.reasoning: Named: Canteen, local independent operators, Vending Exchange free placement, 365 Retail Markets, Cantaloupe micro markets, office pantry/convenience stores

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: 309 x (50% COGS + 10% commission + 5.95% card fee x 80% cashless + 4% shrink = 68.8%) = $213

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Assumed 36-month average placement life: 1 / 36 = 2.8%/month; no source found

expected_lifetime.reasoning: Assumed average placement life before host cancels or swaps operator

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Pitch to signed placement: The Hustle reports 100+ calls for a decent site; assumed 1 in 50 pitches

cac.reasoning: Used machine $2,645 + Nayax reader $314 + $375 prospecting (50 pitches x 0.3 h x $25/h) = $3,334

ltv.reasoning: $309 x 31% x 36 months = $3,448 gross contribution, before fixed costs

payback_months.reasoning: CAC $3,334 / $95.8 monthly contribution per machine = 34.8 months

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Readers 3 x $7.95 + insurance $442/12 + mileage 30 mi/wk x 4.33 x $0.70 = $24 + $37 + $91 = $152

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: $152 fixed / $95.8 contribution per machine = 1.6 machines to cover running costs; ~6 to repay $9,867 capex in 24 months

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 1-2 weeks prospecting + 1 week buying and moving a used machine + 1 week permits and stocking

verdict.cheapest_test: Before buying anything: pitch 40 high-traffic sites in 7 days and get 1 signed placement with 75+ daily users.
kill_criteria: 0 signed placements from 40 pitches by day 7 -> stop
Best site has fewer than 75 daily on-site people -> do not buy a machine
Projected gross under $400/month per machine at day 7 -> do not buy
First full month gross under $250 per machine -> sell the machine within 60 days

rescue.change: Start with 1 combo machine, placed only after a signed deal at a 24/7 warehouse, plant or hospital with 75+ daily staff
rescue.why: Fixes ltv_cac and weak_demand: high-traffic sites gross $400-1,000/month vs ~$309 in offices; keeps $7k in reserve
rescue.requires: 40+ pitches to industrial sites; a signed placement letter before buying

rescue.change: Buy an existing small route with proven locations instead of placing new machines
rescue.why: Fixes channel_readiness and time to revenue: locations and sales history come with it
rescue.requires: Verified sales records, location contracts that transfer, scam screening

narrative.answer: NO-GO at 49. Three snack machines in offices and gyms net about **$137/month** on $9,900 of equipment: a **6-year payback** at under $4/hour of your time, in a shrinking office channel. Only a pre-signed, high-traffic site changes that.
tldr: Base case: 3 machines gross ~$927/month and net ~$137 after stock, commission, card fees and running costs.
$9,867 of used machines pays back in ~72 months, before any repair or a lost site.
Offices sit at ~54% of pre-pandemic occupancy and the US vending market fell 1.3% in 2025.
narrative.lesson: A physical route lives or dies on site traffic; never buy the machine before the site is signed.

key_findings.title: 31% margin before your time
key_findings.detail: After 50% COGS, 10% commission, card fees and 4% shrink, a **$309/month** machine leaves about **$96**.

key_findings.title: Offices half-empty, market shrinking
key_findings.detail: Office occupancy was **54.2%** of pre-pandemic (Jan 2025) and US vending revenue fell **1.3%** in 2025.

key_findings.title: $10,000 buys a 6-year payback
key_findings.detail: 3 used machines at **$2,645** plus readers use the whole budget; the base case nets ~$137/month, so payback is **~72 months**.

narrative.recommendation: Do not buy 3 machines. Spend 7 days pitching 40 warehouses and 24/7 sites; buy one used machine only after a signed placement with 75+ daily users.
narrative.steelman: Snacks are a daily need, there is nothing to build, and a machine in a busy 24/7 site can gross **$400-1,000/month**; routes resell at ~1.16x revenue. The evidence supports that only for high-traffic sites, not typical offices and gyms (~$309).

premortem.cause: Machines gross $150-300/month in hybrid offices and gyms, so the route nets under $150/month.
Weeks of cold pitching find no worthwhile sites; machines sit in the garage.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2 interested sites from 40 pitches

premortem.cause: A host swaps you for Canteen, a micro market or a smart cooler.
premortem.early_signal: Host asks for a higher commission or mentions a micro market within 30 days

changes.what: Office occupancy stuck near half of pre-pandemic levels (54.2% record in Jan 2025).
US vending operator revenue fell 1.3% in 2025 to $7.7bn.
Smart coolers reached 33.5% of deployed equipment, nearly matching glass-front vending.
TikTok and YouTube pushed a wave of new small vending operators.

why_now.note: The office breakroom is shrinking and moving to micro markets while hype adds new small operators: the window is closing.

icp.who: Operations or office manager at a single-site warehouse, plant or 24/7 gym with 75+ daily people and no machine or a neglected one
where: Local chamber of commerce and BNI chapters
LinkedIn: facility and office managers in the metro
icp.pays_for_today: $0: free full-service vending from local or national operators, who often pay the host 5-25% commission
icp.trigger: Current machine is broken, empty or cash-only, or the business moves into a new space

rescue.change: Start with 1 combo machine, placed only after a signed deal at a 24/7 warehouse, plant or hospital with 75+ daily staff
rescue.why: Fixes ltv_cac and weak_demand: high-traffic sites gross $400-1,000/month vs ~$309 in offices; keeps $7k in reserve
rescue.requires: 40+ pitches to industrial sites; a signed placement letter before buying

rescue.change: Buy an existing small route with proven locations instead of placing new machines
rescue.why: Fixes channel_readiness and time to revenue: locations and sales history come with it
rescue.requires: Verified sales records, location contracts that transfer, scam screening

free_alternative.evidence: Consumers pay per vend, so no free product does the job; hosts get vending free from any operator, scored under pricing power.

strong_competitor.evidence: Canteen (Compass Group) runs national vending, markets and pantry; local operators and 365 Retail Markets micro markets pitch the same breakrooms.

graveyard.evidence: A Milwaukee YouTuber spent $6,996 on two machines and had not recovered it after year 1; Fly Vending closed after taking buyer payments (BBB).

no_distribution.evidence: Channel exists: walk-ins and cold calls to hosts. Costly (The Hustle: some operators make 100+ calls per decent site) but credible.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Estimated contribution margin ~31%: 50% COGS, 10% commission, ~4.8% card fees (5.95% rate), 4% shrink.

weak_demand.evidence: IBISWorld: US vending operators -1.3% in 2025 and -0.3%/yr 2020-2025; offices at ~54% of pre-pandemic occupancy.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Searched state permits: sales tax permit and local licence; health permit only for some food. No licence barrier for packaged snacks.

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched TikTok and press hype: a wave of new small operators (Vending Times 2020, 2024) but no countable launches; scored under competitor density.

customer.segment: Office workers and gym members, via the host (office or gym manager)
customer.pain: Wants a snack or drink on site without leaving
customer.today: Existing operator machines, micro markets, office pantries, nearby stores

use_cases.who_pays: Employees per vend; host takes commission

use_cases.effort: Low snack volume, protein drinks sell better

competitors.traction_note: National leader, part of Compass Group

competitors.name: 365 Retail Markets micro markets
competitors.traction_note: Self-described industry leader in unattended retail
competitors.gap: Needs 50+ people and a secure room

competitors.name: Cantaloupe micro markets and smart stores
competitors.traction_note: Public company; ~26,000 US micro market locations
competitors.gap: Operator-facing, not a direct rival for 3 machines

risks.risk: Host removes the machine or switches operator
Used machine breaks; repairs eat a month's profit
risks.mitigation: Buy from dealers with a parts warranty (60 days)
Never prepay for locations; check BBB and FTC history

risks.risk: Sales tax and permit compliance missed
risks.mitigation: Register with the state revenue department before day 1

test_plan.step: List 60 high-traffic sites within 15 miles: warehouses, plants, 24/7 gyms, hospitals
Walk in or call 40 of them; ask for the manager who owns the breakroom
Ask about headcount, shifts and current operator problems
test_plan.verify: 3 or more sites with 75+ daily people and no or poor vending

test_plan.step: Get 2 used-machine quotes and a Nayax quote; model each site's monthly gross
Ask the best site to sign a placement letter
test_plan.verify: 1 signed letter at 10% commission or less
